idiom_name: translator method using Hash#transform_keys/transform_values (or dry-transformer pipelines)
implementation_notes: Ruby's Hash API makes the translator a small method: transform_keys/transform_values/slice/dig express renames, extraction and value normalisation, and key-style differences are one call (transform_keys(&:to_sym)), so the classic translator class collapses into a module method (ruby-doc.org Hash). JSON.parse/JSON.generate (or Oj for speed) own the wire layer, with symbolize_names as the decoding option. The declarative alternative is the dry-transformer gem, whose HashTransform pipelines compose map_keys/rename_keys steps so the mapping is data rather than code; a translator object is justified only when the mapping needs injected lookups.
code_sketch:
module OrderTranslator
  RENAME = { 'order_id' => 'id', 'qty' => 'quantity' }.freeze

  def self.to_canonical(payload)
    h = payload.transform_keys(&:to_s).slice(*RENAME.keys)
    raise InvalidMessage, 'qty' unless h['qty'].to_i.positive?
    h.transform_keys(RENAME).merge('sku' => h['sku'].to_s.strip.upcase)
  end
end
pitfalls: JSON.parse yields string keys unless symbolize_names: true is passed, so a translator written against symbols raises for nil keys instead of finding the field.

transform_keys with no block returns an Enumerator and Hash#each with in-place []= inside a frozen (Ractor-shareable or literal-frozen) payload raises FrozenError; the classic no-op bug is building the renamed hash and then discarding it.
monkey-patching String/Hash helpers into the translator leaks into every other library; keep the mapping inside the module instead of reopening core classes.
